lab_title: The Double Helix Unwound: Structure and Semiconservative Replication of DNA
top_level_objectives: Identify the structural components of the DNA double helix, including sugar-phosphate backbones and nitrogenous bases
Explain how antiparallel strand orientation arises from backbone directionality (5' to 3' vs 3' to 5')
Apply complementary base-pairing rules (A-T, G-C) and describe the hydrogen bonding differences between pairs
Describe the roles of helicase, single-strand binding proteins, DNA polymerase, and DNA ligase in replication
Explain why leading and lagging strand synthesis differ mechanistically, and why this asymmetry is a direct consequence of antiparallel structure
Articulate why DNA replication is described as semiconservative

scenes.brief_purpose: Orient students to the overall 3D shape of DNA before diving into components, building spatial intuition for the helical geometry.
key_visuals: A large rotating semi-transparent double helix model floating above the AR anchor
Two distinctly colored ribbons representing the sugar-phosphate backbones spiraling around a shared central axis
Faint rungs connecting the ribbons suggesting base pairs without detail yet
student_actions: Walk around the projected helix to view it from multiple angles
Use a pinch gesture to rotate and zoom the model
Tap labeled hotspots on the backbone and axis to reveal short tooltip definitions

scenes.brief_purpose: Show students how the chemical directionality of each backbone (5' and 3' ends) explains why the two strands run antiparallel to each other.
key_visuals: Zoomed-in view of a single sugar-phosphate backbone with numbered carbon atoms highlighted on the sugar rings
Color-coded 5' and 3' end labels on both strands pointing in opposite directions
Side-by-side comparison arrows showing the two strands running opposite directions along the same helix
student_actions: Trace a finger along one backbone from the 5' end to the 3' end following a highlighted path
Toggle a comparison view switching between parallel and antiparallel orientations to see why only antiparallel matches real DNA
Answer an embedded quiz prompt identifying the 5' and 3' ends on an unlabeled strand

scenes.brief_purpose: Let students examine the four nitrogenous bases and understand why A pairs with T and G pairs with C, including hydrogen bond counts.
key_visuals: Detailed molecular models of adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine projecting inward from the backbones
Dashed lines representing hydrogen bonds, with two dashed lines between A-T and three between G-C
Color highlighting distinguishing purines (two-ring) from pyrimidines (one-ring)
student_actions: Drag individual base models to attempt pairing them with a complementary base on the opposite strand
Receive visual feedback (snap-fit and glow) when a correct pair is formed, or a bounce-back when incorrect
Count and tap the hydrogen bonds forming between a selected base pair to confirm two vs three bonds

scenes.scene_name: Unwinding the Helix: Helicase and SSBs
scenes.brief_purpose: Transition from static structure to the beginning of replication by showing how the helix is opened at the replication fork.
key_visuals: An animated helicase enzyme model moving along the helix, separating the two strands into a Y-shaped replication fork
Single-strand binding proteins depicted as small beads attaching to and stabilizing the newly exposed single strands
A dynamic label tracking the growing replication bubble
student_actions: Tap the helicase model to trigger its unwinding animation at the fork
Place single-strand binding protein icons onto the exposed single strands to prevent them from re-annealing
Observe and describe in a short response prompt why the exposed strands need stabilization

scenes.scene_name: DNA Polymerase and the Leading Strand
scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce DNA polymerase's synthesis mechanism and show continuous leading strand synthesis in the 5' to 3' direction.
key_visuals: A DNA polymerase enzyme model docking onto the 3' end of a template strand at the replication fork
A new leading strand ribbon extending continuously and smoothly following the moving fork
Directional arrows confirming 5' to 3' synthesis direction on the new strand
student_actions: Drag DNA polymerase onto the correct 3' end of the template strand to initiate leading strand synthesis
Advance a slider or timeline control to watch continuous strand elongation as the fork progresses
Answer a checkpoint question explaining why synthesis can only proceed 5' to 3'

scenes.brief_purpose: Contrast leading strand synthesis with the discontinuous lagging strand synthesis necessitated by antiparallel structure, and show ligase sealing fragments.
key_visuals: The lagging strand template shown running in the opposite direction relative to the fork's movement
Multiple short Okazaki fragment ribbons appearing sequentially with visible gaps between them
A DNA ligase model moving along the lagging strand sealing the gaps into a continuous strand
student_actions: Place successive Okazaki fragments in the correct order as the fork opens further
Drag DNA ligase to each gap between fragments to join them into a continuous strand
Compare a side-by-side animation of leading vs lagging strand synthesis and answer why one is continuous and one is not

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate the entire replication process by showing the final products and reinforcing the semiconservative model.
key_visuals: Two completed daughter double helices floating side by side, each with one strand colored as 'original parental' and one colored as 'newly synthesized'
A split animation replaying the original parental helix separating into the two daughter helices
Summary labels highlighting parental vs new strands in each daughter molecule
student_actions: Tap each daughter helix to highlight which strand is parental and which is newly synthesized
Drag daughter helix labels to match 'semiconservative,' 'conservative,' and 'dispersive' definitions in a matching exercise
Complete a short reflection prompt summarizing why the process is called semiconservative
